$comment: BMW 3 Series E46, the 330i / 330Ci (M54B30) and M3 / M3 CSL (S54B32) trims for Europe (BMW AG data, Germany) and the US (BMW NA). Researched 2026-09-27 from BMW NA technical training manuals (archive.org), BMW AG / GB / NA press kits and spec sheets (press.bmwgroup.com), BMW NA brochures (auto-brochures.com) and the ETK parts catalogue (bmwfans.info mirror). Values are stored as printed: BMW AG weights are the EU figure (DIN + 75 kg driver) except where BMW printed DIN (M3); US weights are BMW NA curb weights. Out of scope: other E46 engines, the 330xi/330xd AWD cars, diesels, the UK-only 330Ci Clubsport, and the Z3 M / Z4 M (S54 in other chassis).

sources.title: BMW of North America press release "BMW M3 - The Variable M Differential Lock" (Munich, 21 Jun 2000)
sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

sources.note: "The new M3 uses the six speed gearbox from the former model and with a 3.62:1 final drive it exceeds 62 mph in second gear."

finalDrive.note: BMW NA printed 3.64:1 from its MY2004 press kit onward (also in the ST041 training manual, the 2004 US brochure and the 2006 kit), after printing 3.62:1 for MY2002-2003 with the same sentence. The parts catalogue (ETK) lists a single final-drive part, 33 10 2 282 480 "I=3,62", for European and US coupes and convertibles and the CSL, with no market or model-year split, so 3.62 is used and 3.64 is treated as a BMW NA documentation discrepancy. Ring and pinion tooth counts were not found.

sources.title: BMW of North America press release "BMW M3 - The Variable M Differential Lock" (Munich, 21 Jun 2000)
sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

curbWeight.method: BMW publishes one weight per body, for the manual car; no SMG II figure was found in BMW AG, BMW GB or BMW NA data. The manual figure is used as a lower bound: the ETK lists the SMG gearbox at 47.8 kg against 46 kg for the manual box, and the SMG hydraulic unit adds more that is not quantified. Base figure: 1495 kg DIN, manual coupe (ST041).

sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

curbWeight.method: No BMW document gives a weight for the Competition Package (US ZCP, German Competition Paket, UK M3 CS). The package swaps the cast 18-inch wheels for forged 19-inch ones, fits CSL front brakes, a 14.5:1 steering rack, M Track Mode and trim; the standard coupe weight is used. Base figure: 1495 kg DIN, manual coupe (ST041).

sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

curbWeight.method: No BMW document gives a weight for the Competition Package (US ZCP, German Competition Paket, UK M3 CS). The package swaps the cast 18-inch wheels for forged 19-inch ones, fits CSL front brakes, a 14.5:1 steering rack, M Track Mode and trim; the standard coupe weight is used. Base figure: 1495 kg DIN, manual coupe (ST041). BMW publishes one weight per body, for the manual car; no SMG II figure was found in BMW AG, BMW GB or BMW NA data. The manual figure is used as a lower bound: the ETK lists the SMG gearbox at 47.8 kg against 46 kg for the manual box, and the SMG hydraulic unit adds more that is not quantified.

finalDrive.note: BMW NA printed 3.64:1 from its MY2004 press kit onward (also in the ST041 training manual, the 2004 US brochure and the 2006 kit), after printing 3.62:1 for MY2002-2003 with the same sentence. The parts catalogue (ETK) lists a single final-drive part, 33 10 2 282 480 "I=3,62", for European and US coupes and convertibles and the CSL, with no market or model-year split, so 3.62 is used and 3.64 is treated as a BMW NA documentation discrepancy. sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

curbWeight.method: BMW publishes one weight per body, for the manual car; no SMG II figure was found in BMW AG, BMW GB or BMW NA data. The manual figure is used as a lower bound: the ETK lists the SMG gearbox at 47.8 kg against 46 kg for the manual box, and the SMG hydraulic unit adds more that is not quantified. Base figure: 3415 lb, manual coupe (BMW NA). Car and Driver measured 3,508 lb on an optioned SMG coupe against 3,440 lb for a manual test car.

weightFrontPercent.method: BMW NA publishes the 50.3/49.7 split for the M3 coupe without distinguishing SMG II; the manual figure is used.

finalDrive.note: BMW NA printed 3.64:1 from its MY2004 press kit onward (also in the ST041 training manual, the 2004 US brochure and the 2006 kit), after printing 3.62:1 for MY2002-2003 with the same sentence. The parts catalogue (ETK) lists a single final-drive part, 33 10 2 282 480 "I=3,62", for European and US coupes and convertibles and the CSL, with no market or model-year split, so 3.62 is used and 3.64 is treated as a BMW NA documentation discrepancy. Ring and pinion tooth counts were not found.

sources.note: "generates pressure spontaneously in an integrated shear pump. This pressure is then conveyed via a piston to a multiple-plate clutch, thereby channeling power to the wheel with better grip."

differential.note: BMW's "variable M differential lock", developed with GKN Viscodrive: a sealed shear pump (about 46 g of silicone fluid) builds pressure in proportion to the left-right wheel-speed difference; a piston (max. 38 bar) clamps multi-plate clutches. Earlier M cars used a torque-sensing LSD with a 25% lock value (ST041 p. 10). BMW says that in an extreme case all drive power can go to one wheel; no preload or lock curve is published. 210 mm ring gear.

curbWeight.method: BMW publishes one weight per body, for the manual car; no SMG II figure was found in BMW AG, BMW GB or BMW NA data. The manual figure is used as a lower bound: the ETK lists the SMG gearbox at 47.8 kg against 46 kg for the manual box, and the SMG hydraulic unit adds more that is not quantified. Base figure: 3781 lb, manual convertible (BMW NA).

weightFrontPercent.method: BMW NA publishes the 49.9/50.1 split for the M3 convertible without distinguishing SMG II; the manual figure is used.
